refs.description: Motion to set aside information — follows the preliminary hearing. The § 995 motion attacks the hold-to-answer order based on insufficiency of the probable cause evidence. Cross-reference pen_code_995_motion_to_dismiss.

Brady/Giglio discovery — prosecution's disclosure obligations apply from arraignment forward. Brady demand should be served immediately after arraignment; information revealed at prelim hearing may trigger additional Brady obligations. Cross-reference pen_code_1054_1_discovery.

Hearsay admissibility at preliminary hearing — Prop 115 rule allowing law enforcement to testify to hearsay. Companion section to § 859. Understanding § 872(b) is required to develop the cross-examination strategy for a one-witness prelim.

Pitchess motion — if APD officers testify at the preliminary hearing, Pitchess discovery of their personnel records may be sought before or during the preliminary hearing. Cross-reference pen_code_1054_1_discovery for Pitchess overlay.

Good cause for continuance — the standard for continuing a preliminary hearing beyond the 10-court-day limit. Prosecution must establish good cause. Defense should object to continuances that are not justified.

Confrontation Clause — preliminary hearing creates early confrontation rights issues. Where a witness testifies at the prelim and later becomes unavailable, their prelim testimony may be admitted at trial only if the defendant had an opportunity to cross-examine. This makes aggressive prelim cross-examination critical.

Where the coordinated false accusation theory is operative, the preliminary hearing is the venue to begin establishing that the arrest was procured through coordination. Cross-examination of the APD officer about the call-in time, caller identity, and pre-positioning is the foundation of the § 182(a)(2) conspiracy theory. Cross-reference pen_code_182_conspiracy.
